evidence.claim: China announced export controls on tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum, and indium related items in February 2025.
evidence.source_title: China announces export controls on items related to tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum, indium

evidence.claim: The IEA policy tracker records China's Decision No. 10 of 2025 implementing export controls on certain tungsten-related and other items under export-control and customs laws.
evidence.source_title: Decision to implement export controls on tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum and indium related items

evidence.claim: Almonty announced completion of Phase 1 commissioning at the Sangdong Tungsten Mine in South Korea in March 2026, with the plant designed for roughly 2,300 tonnes of tungsten concentrate per year in Phase 1 and a planned Phase 2 increase to roughly 4,600 tonnes per year.
evidence.source_title: Almonty Completes Phase 1 of Sangdong Tungsten Mine in South Korea

evidence.claim: Almonty's July 2025 F-10 filing stated that it expected Sangdong production in the second half of 2025, had secured offtake for a significant proportion of expected Phase I production, and was assessing downstream tungsten oxide processing in South Korea.

Kennametal's SEC filing describes products including tungsten carbide powders for aerospace and process industries, high-temperature critical wear components, tungsten penetrators, and armor solutions for aerospace and defense.
evidence.source_title: Kennametal Inc. Form 10-Q for quarter ended December 31, 2025

evidence.claim: Kennametal's company materials identify advanced materials for protective armor and mission-critical defense components as part of its business profile.
Ajinomoto describes Ajinomoto Build-up Film as an insulating film used in semiconductor package substrates for high-performance semiconductors.

Ajinomoto stated in a company press release that ABF is primarily used as an interlayer insulating material in semiconductor package substrates for computers and had top share in its field, mainly for CPU applications.
evidence.source_title: Ajinomoto Co., Inc. Starts Operation to Strengthen Its Electronic Materials Business Ajinomoto Fine-Techno USA Corporation

evidence.claim: MEC's medium-term business plan describes its CZ-series adhesion promoter as a copper surface treatment agent that enhances adhesion between copper and resin by forming a unique uneven shape with low etching amount.
MEC lists electronic-substrate chemicals and copper surface treatment products, supporting its mapping to the specialty chemistry node of the package-substrate chain.
Federal Reserve research using earnings-call text analysis found that firm commentary can provide timely information about supply bottlenecks and pricing pressure across industries.
evidence.source_title: Effects of Supply Chain Bottlenecks on Prices using Textual Analysis

evidence.claim: For the 'New Hotspots' funnel, earnings-call references to allocation, lead times, customer qualification, and pricing should be used as repeatable evidence signals for substrate materials, tungsten processing, and recycling nodes.
evidence.source_title: Effects of Supply Chain Bottlenecks on Prices using Textual Analysis

evidence.claim: Cached Layer 1 Serenity context identified tungsten and AI advanced-packaging substrates/materials as candidate 'New Hotspots' source nodes; this Layer 2A map treats those as the starting funnel rather than final validated conclusions.

memory_update.text: Track 'China tungsten export licensing and controlled-material policy' as a primary regulatory node for the New Hotspots theme.

APT/tungsten oxide/downstream conversion may be a stronger chokepoint than tungsten mining alone because concentrate must become qualified material for defense, aerospace, tooling, and other customers.
ABF insulating film, high-layer FC-BGA substrate yield, and copper adhesion/surface-treatment chemistry should be tracked as hidden AI packaging bottlenecks below the obvious GPU/HBM layer.
Defense-compliant tungsten powder, carbide, penetrators, and armor components are embedded in broader industrial tooling and engineered-material companies; do not map only pure-play miners.
Tungsten recycling and scrap traceability outside China should be added as a distribution/relief-valve node, especially if primary non-China supply ramps slower than policy-driven demand.

Use Sangdong shipped volumes, recovery rates, concentrate quality, customer acceptance, and downstream oxide facility progress as catalysts/falsification signals for the allied tungsten supply thesis.

Use substrate maker utilization, ABF allocation commentary, material lead times, gross margin, and qualification wins as catalysts/falsification signals for the AI packaging-material chokepoint thesis.
Need direct filing-level verification for Kinsus, Unimicron, Ibiden, AT&S, and other substrate makers: AI/HPC substrate revenue mix, customer concentration, yield, utilization, and capex timing.
Need direct evidence on MEC's current revenue exposure to FC-BGA/HBM/AI package substrate applications and whether its copper surface-treatment products are capacity- or qualification-constrained.
Need legal-source confirmation of latest U.S. defense procurement restrictions and effective dates for tungsten, recycled tungsten exceptions, and contractor flowdown requirements.

Need mapping of underfollowed distributors, brokers, recyclers, and qualified processors in the tungsten chain; current evidence is stronger for miners and industrial materials companies than for distribution nodes.

Avoid letting high-attention mega-cap AI chip vendors and defense primes dominate this theme map; the working chokepoint hypothesis lives in upstream material qualification, process chemistry, conversion capacity, and regulated sourcing gates.

summary: Layer 2A maps 'New Hotspots' as a two-cluster emerging chokepoint theme rather than a single ticker theme: (1) China-linked critical-mineral control valves, especially tungsten for defense, aerospace, hard metals, and semiconductor-adjacent uses; and (2) AI advanced-packaging capacity constraints, especially high-layer FC-BGA/ABF substrates and niche copper-surface-treatment chemistry. The highest bottleneck nodes are not the obvious AI accelerator or defense prime end-customers, but upstream/embedded nodes with long qualification cycles: non-China tungsten concentrate-to-APT/oxide conversion, defense-compliant tungsten powder/carbide/penetrator supply, ABF insulating film, high-layer substrate yield/capacity, and specialty adhesion/surface chemistry used by package substrate manufacturers. This is research mapping only, not a trading recommendation.

supply_chain_map.node: AI accelerator and HBM package demand
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Large AI accelerator packages require advanced substrates, HBM integration, high-density interconnect, and CoWoS-like packaging flows; demand shocks can propagate into less-followed substrate materials and process chemicals.

supply_chain_map.node: High-layer FC-BGA and AI/HPC package substrates
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Substrates are harder to scale than simple PCB capacity because yield, layer count, warpage control, customer qualification, and capex timing matter; underfollowed substrate makers can be hidden one layer below GPU/HBM narratives.

supply_chain_map.node: ABF insulating film for advanced semiconductor packages
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: ABF is a critical insulating material in high-performance package substrates. It is a high-leverage material node because many AI/HPC substrate designs depend on it even when the public-market attention is on chip vendors or memory vendors.

supply_chain_map.node: Copper surface treatment and adhesion chemistry for IC substrates
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Niche chemicals that improve copper-resin adhesion and high-frequency substrate performance can become yield and reliability gates. These suppliers may be overlooked because they screen as small specialty chemical companies rather than AI infrastructure suppliers.

Qualification by substrate makers and semiconductor packaging customers can create switching costs and long validation cycles. This can hide bottleneck value in process chemicals, materials, and substrate makers with proven customer access.

supply_chain_map.node: China tungsten export licensing and controlled-material policy
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: China's 2025 tungsten-related export controls turn tungsten from a commodity input into a policy-sensitive supply node. Licensing discretion can raise the value of non-China supply, recycling, and qualified processing routes.

Non-China mine supply is the upstream feedstock gate for allied tungsten chains. Production ramp timing, grade, recoveries, and offtake performance determine whether policy-driven demand can translate into physical supply.

supply_chain_map.node: APT, tungsten oxide, and downstream conversion capacity
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: The chain does not end at concentrate. Defense, semiconductor-adjacent, and tooling customers often need processed tungsten intermediates or powders, so conversion capacity can be a bigger chokepoint than mining headlines.

supply_chain_map.node: Defense-compliant tungsten powder, carbide, penetrators, and armor components
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Defense applications require traceable, qualified materials. Public-market exposure may hide inside industrial tooling and engineered-materials companies rather than pure-play miners.

supply_chain_map.node: Tungsten recycling and scrap collection outside China
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: If primary non-China supply is slow to scale, compliant scrap collection and recycling could become a short-cycle relief valve. The bottleneck may be collection, traceability, refining capability, and whether recycled material qualifies under procurement rules.

supply_chain_map.node: Defense procurement sourcing restrictions and contractor flowdowns
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Rules restricting covered materials from certain countries can force primes and subcontractors to requalify supply chains. The economic value may accrue to companies that can document compliant origin and processing.

supply_chain_map.node: Specialty industrial distributors and qualified material brokers
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: In policy-sensitive shortages, less-visible distributors may control allocation, documentation, and customer access. This node is likely under-mapped and requires follow-up source work.

supply_chain_map.node: Metallurgical processing equipment for tungsten mine and mill ramps
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: New mine supply depends on mills, flotation/gravity circuits, commissioning, recoveries, and plant uptime. Equipment is a second-order node, but ramp failure would falsify upstream supply claims.

supply_chain_map.node: AI data-center rack-level power and memory-adjacent components
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: AI infrastructure demand can spill into MLCCs, high-capacity memory, SSD/HDD allocation, and power-delivery components. This node is included as a watchlist extension but is less evidenced in the current Layer 2A package than tungsten and packaging materials.
